title: Make billing answerable without a support ticket, by Fri 27 Nov
description: The app has plan pickers, invoices and a cancellation modal, but nothing public explains invoices, receipts, VAT, failed payments, refunds, or who to contact when billing breaks. Write the page from the actual screens, so each answer names the exact place the action lives. Cover: where an invoice is found, what a receipt looks like, whether VAT is charged, what happens when a card fails, how a refund is requested, and what changing plan mid-term costs. Point every uncertain answer at the person who can confirm it.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Document the failure paths, because that is what support actually gets
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Nobody writes to support because a payment succeeded. Work: establish what happens on a declined card, an expired card, a failed renewal, a removed payment method and a plan change that cannot be charged — what the customer sees, whether access continues, and what the system retries. Where this cannot be tested safely, get it from the billing code and name the file. Deliver the failure table, the customer-facing explanation for each, and the note on any case where the app currently says nothing at all.

upvotes.reason: Anchoring 'Make billing answerable without a support ticket, by Fri 27 Nov' in verified operational workflows accelerates cohort onboarding.

Support tickets come from failure paths, not the happy path. Documenting those paths is the shortest route to fewer tickets.
Declines, expired cards and failed renewals are what support actually receives; documenting them is more useful than describing the happy path.
Support tickets are almost all failure paths; documenting declined, expired and refunded payments answers the questions the happy path never raises.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Explain plan changes with a worked example using the real prices
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The question behind most billing tickets is "what will I be charged if I change now". Work: take the real monthly prices, build four examples — upgrade mid-month, downgrade mid-month, change on the renewal date, and cancel and return — and show the arithmetic in the same terms the invoice uses. Then check the app agrees, or state where it does not. Deliver the four examples, the arithmetic, the screen where each happens, and the sentence to publish so a customer can predict the next invoice.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Open a real invoice and check it contains what the page will claim
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Every billing page eventually says "your invoice shows X". Work: open a real invoice and receipt as a customer sees them and record every field: plan name, period, currency, tax line, amount, company details, invoice number, and what is missing. Then write the page against that evidence and list the fields that should exist but do not. Deliver the field-by-field table, the page copy, and the list of invoice changes worth raising with whoever owns billing, separately from the page.

The page will claim what the invoice shows, so it has to be written from an actual invoice. Listing the real fields first prevents copy that describes a document the customer never receives.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Publish who to contact and what to include when billing breaks, and hold that address to a stated reply time
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A billing problem is urgent in a way other support is not, so the path has to be short and the expectation explicit. Work: name the route, the information the customer should include (workspace, invoice number, last four digits, the exact message), and the reply time the team can actually meet. Then test the route once and record how long the first reply took. Deliver the published block, the internal checklist for whoever answers, and the measured first-reply time compared to the promise.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Walk every billing screen and write each answer from the screen it lives on
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Help pages fail when they describe a screen that has moved. Deliver the screen inventory with the answer attached to each, plus the three screens where the label does not match what the button does.
